sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Reading the feature list file
sections.what: Loads the feature list file next to the script and reads it as data. Nothing is shown yet; this is the setup step before any checks run.
sections.why: Likely reason: the feature list is the single record of progress, so it must be read first. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the file is missing or not valid JSON, the script stops with a raw error before any checks run.

sections.name: errors
sections.title: Rule checks for each feature
sections.what: Goes through each feature and collects every rule it breaks: a missing field, a duplicate id, an empty acceptance list, a passing value that is not true or false, or a passing feature with too little evidence. Unknown dependencies are always reported, but a dependency that is not passing is reported only when the feature depending on it claims to pass.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops features from being marked done without proof and keeps the list consistent.
sections.watch_out: A feature still in progress can list a dependency that is not finished without triggering a dependency error.

sections.name: phases
sections.title: Summary and final result
sections.what: Counts passing features overall and per phase, prints those counts, then prints any collected errors and stops with failure if there are any. The counts print even when errors exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary gives a quick progress view, and the failure exit lets other tools fail the check. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Phase groups come from whatever phase names appear in the list, so a misspelled phase creates a new group instead of an error.

summary: A small checker that reads the feature list, reports how many features pass overall and by phase, and fails if the list breaks its rules.
purpose: Keeps the record of finished features honest, so a feature counts as passing only with evidence and with passing dependencies.
why: Likely reason: progress claims need proof. The header comment states the goal of validating the list.
how: Reads the feature list file next to it. Checks each feature for required fields, a non-empty acceptance list, a true or false passing value, and evidence of at least 20 characters when passing. Checks that ids are unique and dependencies exist, and that a passing feature does not depend on a feature that is not passing. Prints totals and per-phase counts, then exits with failure if any errors were collected.
inputs: The feature_list.json file in the same folder, containing a features list whose entries have the required fields.
outputs: Printed progress counts and any error messages. Exit code 0 when clean, 1 when there are errors.
risks: A missing or malformed file stops the script with a raw error. The only check on proof is evidence length, so weak text can pass. Circular dependencies are not detected. A feature without a depends_on field would make the script crash.
debug: Read each error; it names the feature id. If the script crashes, check that the file is valid JSON and every feature has all required fields. If counts look wrong, check the passes values.
